commits.message: perf(sources): a key or depends_on policy compares what it read by value, so an input that moved without moving it hashes nothing (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8e9)
perf(sources): a registry's runs are observed for its life, so a turn in which nothing moved derives them nothing again (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8e9)
fix(check): a prepared config closes its runs with its registry, so the gallery leaks no hold, period or watch past its draw (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8e9)
fix(check): a run that moved nothing answers the same fact, so a re-bind publishes nothing again (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8e9)
fix(collector): a run whose declaration throws fails that run alone, and every other lane of the session declares (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8e9)

fix(renderer): a request waits on every run its view names, so a run whose key lands after the request arrived is waited on (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8e9)

The world state carries only runs the host has subscribed, and the host
subscribes a moved key's run a turn after the world state that moved it.
The wait now reads the view's named runs too, and the test host hands
subscriptions back after the answer settles, as the real host does.

feat(host): the host runs shell and file sources from the renderer's subscriptions, and their readings come back in the world state (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.8e9)

A view's registry names each shell and file source's run as a digest of its
identity, and the renderer's output subscribes to those runs. The collector
holds them through the daemon's one SourceRuns, and each session's world state
carries their readings, so a run is read once for every session naming it and
the registry holds no runs of its own. Shell and file variables are now
view-scoped. A run's identity is derived from its policy's inputs, never
written by a reaction, so a turn reading subscriptions mid-batch names the run
the move just produced. Unheld runs keep their last answer up to a bound.
